title: Psycholinguistic Features of Listening Comprehension as a Type of Speech Activity
content: This article deals with the psychological features of listening comprehension as a type of speech activity. The psychological nature of listening comprehension as a process is analyzed, and the levels and mechanisms of speech perception and understanding described in the psycholinguistic literature are examined, including Friedrich Kainz's model of speech understanding. It is argued that the problem of perceiving a foreign language by ear is of considerable importance both for the methodology of foreign language teaching and for psychology and linguistics, since different aspects of the problem are studied by different sciences. The article concludes that listening comprehension is a perceptual, mental, and mnemonic activity and, as such, is one of the most complex types of speech activity, requiring systematic and purposeful development in foreign-language instruction.
